observations.text: SP, due to an incomplete use of the navigation computer during mission planning, did not produce the leg headings, times and fuel figures required by the mission planning sheets before the briefing. The IP had to direct the recomputation and execute part of the planning. The ground procedures were not completed without assistance.

SP, due to mission planning that did not address the forecast weather at the recovery time, did not plan the alternative mission and did not raise the recovery option during the briefing conducted according to the Mission Briefing Guide. The IP had to select the alternative route and complete the fuel plan. The ground procedures were not completed without assistance and the planning sequence is to be repeated under supervision.

SP completed the ground procedures at the desired standard for this Training Unit, with the mission planning sheets and the Before Taxiing checks accomplished after the IP's verbal prompts. Two leg times entered from the navigation computer were recognized as erroneous and corrected with delay, and no procedure of the LAP or the SOPs was skipped once prompted. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a self-initiated planning and checklist flow is expected in the following sorties.

SP planned the navigation mission according to A/C energy planning and his training level, with minor errors in the fuel checkpoint figures of the mission planning sheets, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. All checks were executed according to the checklist and the specified taxi route was followed with the ground path kept clear of obstacles. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed all checks according to the checklist, without IP's intervention, in an impeccable and standardized manner, and took part in the mission briefing according to the Mission Briefing Guide with the route, the fuel plan and the alternative mission presented accurately. Cooperation with the ground crew was conducted without allowing mis-apprehensions and the A/C was stopped as required without oscillations. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, applying an accurate and standardized flow between the aeronautical maps, the navigation computer and the mission planning sheets, planned the primary navigation route and the alternative mission and briefed both according to the Mission Briefing Guide. Every normal procedure of the Flight Manual, the Local Area Procedures and the SOPs was executed without omission and without IP's intervention, with correct use of all A/C levers and switches. The A/C condition was specified and its flight permissibility decided correctly and confidently at the walk-around. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect technique of transferring the leg data to the aeronautical map without a back-check against the mission planning sheets, did not verify the turning points before the briefing, leaving two legs plotted on wrong coordinates. The IP had to direct the correction and execute part of the planning. The ground procedures were not completed without assistance.

SP, due to lack of awareness of a published restriction that was available in the briefing material, planned the route through an area active at the sortie time and did not identify it during the briefing conducted according to the Mission Briefing Guide. The IP had to direct the re-planning of the affected legs and completed the fuel recomputation. The ground procedures were not completed without assistance.

SP, due to a non-standardized checklist flow, did not perform the Before Taxiing checks in the prescribed sequence, leaving the navigation equipment items unverified. The checks were completed only after the IP's verbal prompts and the omission was recognized and corrected with delay at the holding point.

SP, due to workload management that left the map preparation unfinished before the step time, did not have the route legs and the fuel checkpoints ready when the ground procedures commenced. The remaining planning items were completed only after the IP's verbal prompts during the start sequence, and the shortfall was recognized with delay. Cooperation with the ground crew was maintained, but the sequence prescribed by the LAP and the SOPs was not respected.

SP performed the ground procedures within the desired standards, with the planning of the navigation route, the briefing and all checks accomplished without IP's intervention. Two fuel checkpoint figures on the mission planning sheets were re-computed before they were accepted, and one deviation from the specified taxi route was corrected by SP. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency in the planning flow and in taxi route discipline is expected to improve.

SP executed all checks according to the checklist, without IP's intervention, in an impeccable and standardized manner, and specified the A/C condition and its flight permissibility correctly and confidently. The navigation route and the alternative mission were planned according to A/C energy planning and briefed according to the Mission Briefing Guide, and the frequency checks were completed on the ground before taxi. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, having planned the navigation mission according to A/C energy planning and his training level, briefed the route, the fuel checkpoints and the alternative mission according to the Mission Briefing Guide without omission. All normal procedures of the Flight Manual, the LAP and the SOPs were executed without IP's intervention and with correct use of all A/C levers and switches, the ground crew position being verified before every switch actuation. The specified taxi route was followed and the A/C was stopped as required without oscillations. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect technique in the use of the A/C levers and switches during the navigation equipment setup, did not complete the Before Taxiing checks according to the Flight Manual, leaving the route data unloaded. The IP had to interrupt the sequence and execute part of the procedure before taxi. The ground procedures were not completed without assistance.

SP, due to failure to pass the required call at the briefed point, did not execute the frequency checks on the ground before taxi and did not confirm the navigation and inter-flight frequencies according to the pre-flight briefing. The IP had to direct the frequency selections and complete the check. The ground procedures were not completed without assistance and the briefed radio sequence is to be repeated under supervision.

SP, due to an unstructured cross-check between the mission planning sheets and the aeronautical map, did not verify the leg times and the fuel checkpoints against the A/C energy planning before the briefing. The figures were corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts and the discrepancy was recognized with delay.

SP, due to complacency on a route flown repeatedly without incident, did not study the current restrictions and the LAP items applicable to the navigation area during the ground preparation. The omission was covered only after the IP's verbal prompts at the briefing, with recognition and correction delayed. No consequence to the conduct of the sortie resulted, but the ground procedures were not completed independently.

SP, due to a late power reduction while taxiing as No2, did not keep the standard distance from the leader and stopped the A/C with two slight oscillations at the last chance area. The deviation was minor and was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. All remaining checks were executed according to the checklist and no procedure of the LAP or the SOPs was skipped.

SP, due to distraction from the primary task by an unrelated switch action during the start sequence, delayed the frequency checks on the ground beyond the point briefed for them. The outstanding check was identified by SP and completed in a timely manner before taxi, without IP's intervention. The error was minor and did not affect the mission planning or the assessment of the A/C flight permissibility.

SP executed the ground procedures within the desired standards, accomplishing the mission planning, the briefing and all checks according to the checklist without IP's intervention. The preparation of the map and of the mission planning sheets was slower than the standard for this unit and two fuel figures were re-checked before the route was accepted. Marginal performance for the Training Section - speed in the ground preparation is expected to improve while the present accuracy is maintained.

SP planned the navigation mission and the alternative mission according to A/C energy planning and his training level, and briefed both according to the Mission Briefing Guide with every threat of the route identified. Every check was executed according to the checklist, without IP's intervention and without omitting any procedure of the LAP or the SOPs, and the frequency checks were completed on the ground before taxi, timely and correctly. The specified taxi route was followed with the standard distance from the leader kept during taxi and the ground path continuously verified clear of obstacles. Above end of block MIF achieved.
